title: Cryo-EM Structure of Infective Sindbis Virus at 3.1 Å Resolution Reveals Insights into Alphavirus Host-Cell Entry and Assembly
content: Alphaviruses are enveloped RNA viruses that include several human pathogens. Despite their significant impact on human health, a high-resolution structure of the alphavirus virion has been lacking due to the intrinsic heterogeneity of these particles. Here, we present the cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structure of the infective Sindbis virus at a resolution of 3.1 Å, obtained using a local-based reconstruction method that overcomes the challenges posed by particle heterogeneity. Our structural analysis reveals several conserved residues that are crucial to the viral life cycle, including a hydrophobic pocket in the subdomain D of the E2 protein, which is stabilized by an unidentified pocket factor near the viral membrane. The conserved nature of these residues across different alphaviruses suggests a potential target for antiviral interventions. The identified hydrophobic pocket strengthens the interactions between the E1/E2 heterodimer and may play a key role in virus assembly. We also analyze the post-translational modifications in the Sindbis virus. Especially the glycosylation residues in E1 and E2 that may affect host receptor binding and immune evasion, particularly at N196 and N318 positions in the E2 domain. Additionally, our study provides insights into alphavirus host-cell entry and assembly mechanisms, which are essential for the rational design of antiviral drugs and vaccines. The structural information provided here offers a foundation for further exploration of alphavirus biology and supports efforts toward targeted therapeutic development.
